# Introduction

R is a programming language designed primarily for statistical computing, data analysis, and visualization.

This chapter introduces the basic syntax and operations used in R.

# Variables and Assignment

R commonly uses `<-` operator for assignment.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- 10
name <- "Sujan"
is_human <- TRUE
salary <- 0.1
```
:::


We can then inspect these values:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 10
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
name
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Sujan"
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
is_human
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] TRUE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
salary
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.1
```


:::
:::


## Assignment Operator

We can also use `=` operator for assignment:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x = 20
x
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 20
```


:::
:::


However, `<-` is the most conventional assignment operator in R.

# Arithmetic Operators


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
10 + 5
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 15
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10 - 5
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 5
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10 * 5
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 50
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10 / 5
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 2
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10^2
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 100
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10 %% 3
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 1
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
10 %/% 3
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 3
```


:::
:::


| Operator | Meaning            |
|----------|--------------------|
| `+`      | Addition           |
| `-`      | Subtraction        |
| `*`      | Multiplication     |
| `/`      | Division           |
| `^`      | Exponentiation     |
| `%%`     | Modulo / remainder |
| `%/%`    | Integer division   |

# Comments

Comments begin with `#`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# This is a comment

x <- 10 # This assigns 10 to x
```
:::


# Getting Help

R has extensive built-in documentation.

```         
?mean
```

You can also use:

```         
help(mean)
```

To search for a topic:

```         
??regression
```

# Basic Output

Use `print()` to explicitly print a value.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
print("Hello R!")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "Hello R!"
```


:::
:::


However, R can also display an expression directly:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- 30
x
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 30
```


:::
:::


# Checking the working Directory


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
getwd()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "D:/R/r-programming-handbook/lessons"
```


:::
:::


Change it when necessary:

```         
setwd("path/to/directory")
```
> **Recommendation:** When working with RStudio Projects, prefer project-relative paths instead of repeatedly using `setwd()`.

# Quick Reference

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<-` | Assignment |
| `print()` | Print a value |
| `getwd()` | Get working directory |
| `setwd()` | Change working directory |
| `?function` | Open function documentation |
| `help()` | Open documentation |
| `??term` | Search documentation |
| `#` | Comment |
